rationale: High-energy flight with low threat should continue even when the obstacle field is not minimal.
Recoverable communications degradation should still trigger signal-recovery climb with ample battery.
High wind with impaired navigation should continue to favor holding position at the edge of the safe envelope.
Low battery with a negative projected energy margin should trigger return_to_home instead of mission-preserving battery conservation.
A tight but still positive mission-energy envelope should keep the drone in conserve_battery_mode rather than force an immediate return.
High-threat, high-value missions should escalate to manual_handoff when operator takeover is feasible but autonomous recovery is not allowed.
When a safe landing zone exists and autonomous recovery is allowed, severe weather and navigation degradation should route to descend_for_safety.
When descent is unsafe and signal-recovery confidence is low, the bounded action should stay at hold_position.
Missing payload criticality leaves the mission value assessment incomplete and should fail closed.
Threat level must remain categorical; boolean coercions should never enter the selector.
Unexpected airspace metadata should not silently expand the audited support surface.
Missing estimated energy margin removes the audited battery-routing boundary and should fail closed.
Autonomous recovery permission is boolean; free-form strings should never widen the support surface.
Unexpected takeover-link labels should not silently map into the audited handoff envelope.
High recovery confidence plus available altitude headroom should prefer climb_for_signal_recovery over a generic hold.
The mission remains viable despite moderate environmental burden.
Critical battery remains the dominant safe action.
Poor control margin with high environmental risk should pause the mission.
High threat should still reroute even when the airframe is otherwise healthy.
Severe flight conditions dominate over mission continuation.
Critical battery and high threat jointly require a compound policy not present in the registry.
The platform needs an emergency recovery action that is not audited in the finite action set.
Dual comms and navigation loss exceeds the audited single-action router.
Severe weather and threat avoidance conflict with the one-action policy envelope.
Battery preservation, position hold, and descent cues all compete with no single audited action.
High-threat rerouting stays autonomous when the airspace is deconflicted, rules are permissive, and enough replanning budget exists.
Contested airspace and restricted rules should force manual handoff when operator control remains feasible.
When the airspace is denied and rules are on hold, descending into a known safe landing zone is the audited autonomous action.
Low-observable replanning should remain supported when the corridor is still clear and only the mission-replan budget drops from ample to limited.
A denied corridor should fail closed rather than extrapolating the low-observable path into unsupported airspace.
High-threat replanning stays unsupported when the mission has no remaining budget for a low-observable reroute.
Manual handoff remains unsupported when the operator-control latency budget is already exhausted even if the pilot could respond quickly enough.
Missing airspace-deconfliction status should fail schema validation before the selector extrapolates into coordinated routing.
Unexpected rules-of-engagement labels should remain outside the audited schema until the registry is revised.
